checked.evidence: Endorsed by the OSMF board 2014-06-06. Verbatim: 'If you use OpenStreetMap data along with non-OpenStreetMap data for a given Feature Type, then the share-alike condition would apply regardless of whether some data for that Feature Type is in a different layer than the other data for that Feature Type.' Worked example is exactly the complement-the-gaps dedup case: 'if there are restaurants in the OpenStreetMap layer and you add additional restaurants in another layer, but you include only those restaurants not present in the OpenStreetMap layer... the restaurants added in your non-OpenStreetMap layer must be shared.' The researcher's quote is accurate to the character. One scoping nuance: the guideline's own preamble frames it as 'primarily relat[ing] to making and publicly publishing visual 2D maps, (a "Produced Work"...)', though the operative Feature-Type rule is stated generally.

Doubled 'Guideline_Guideline' in the path is the genuine page title (oldid=3980), not a typo. Verbatim example: 'You have a proprietary list of restaurants for a country. You would like to complement your list with the corresponding data from OpenStreetMap removing any duplicate objects in the process. The resulting, combined database would not be covered by this guideline and you would, if the dataset is publicly used, have to consider that your proprietary data may be subject to the ODbL share-alike terms.' Operative rule confirmed: combination stays a Collective Database 'so long as the data used for a particular data type is either all OSM or all non-OSM within the same regional cut'. Also confirms 'Two data sets need not be physically separated to qualify as "independent"' — i.e. per-Feature-Type purity, not schema separation, is the actual test. This validates the repo's existing CHECK constraint present_in <@ ARRAY['overture','fsq'] as the thing actually doing the legal work.

Full licence text present. §4.4 'Share alike', §4.5 'Limits of Share Alike' with 4.5(b) 'Using this Database... to create a Produced Work does not create a Derivative Database for purposes of Section 4.4', and §4.6 'Access to Derivative Databases... a copy in a machine readable form of: a. The entire Derivative Database' — all three section numbers cited by the researcher are correct.
checked.correction: The researcher's fallback advice ('if ODbL route geometry must be used, restrict output to ODbL §4.5 Produced Works') is materially incomplete and would mislead the build. §4.4(c), which the researcher did not cite, closes that escape hatch: 'A Derivative Database is Publicly Used and so must comply with Section 4.4. if a Produced Work created from the Derivative Database is Publicly Used.' So if route-buffer joins create a Derivative Database internally, publishing ANY public map/page from it triggers share-alike on the database itself plus the §4.6 duty to hand over a machine-readable copy. The Produced-Work carve-out only protects you where no Derivative Database was formed in the first place. This strengthens rather than weakens the recommendation to source routes from public-domain federal geometry.

Transportation = ODbL is likewise confirmed, which independently validates the warning against deriving the routes table from Overture Transportation.

§11 duty CONFIRMED verbatim: 'If you are downloading individual images and serving them from your own servers, you must attribute the image(s) by visibly displaying the Mapillary logo and linking back to the Mapillary homepage or corresponding Mapillary image page.' checked.correction: Two defects in the researcher's flat claim license='CC BY-SA (user-contributed imagery), per ToS §3(b)'. (1) The licence is NOT uniformly CC BY-SA — the same sentence continues 'unless we indicate otherwise. For instance, we may provide access to certain User Content (alone or in combination with other data sets) under a separate set of license terms (such as the Creative Commons Attribution NonCommercial Share Alike (CC BY-NC-SA license)'. Some Mapillary imagery is therefore NON-COMMERCIAL-restricted, so a blanket 'CC BY-SA' entry in the source register is a licence misstatement of exactly the damaging kind; per-image licence must be read at fetch time. (2) The pinpoint cite is off — the CC BY-SA sentence sits in the §3 licence grant, which cross-refers to §3(b) for a different restriction. Additionally the researcher missed §12 'Use of the Mapillary Services for Commercial Purposes', which imposes further terms limiting commercial use to an enumerated list.

checked.evidence: Extra check I ran to test the researcher's 'Overture has no rating field' assertion rather than accept it. Schema field list is: geometry (Point), sources[], operating_status, categories (basic_category/taxonomy), confidence, websites, socials, emails, phones, brand, addresses (freeform/locality/postcode/region/country), names. There is NO rating and NO review-count field — assertion holds. 'confidence' is documented as 'A score between 0 and 1 indicating how confident we are that the place exists', explicitly a record-existence score, which validates the researcher's warning never to relabel it as a customer rating. Also confirms phones/emails/websites/socials and postcode DO exist, so the proposed fallbacks are real. CAVEAT the researcher did not flag: no opening-hours field appears in this schema reference, so the requested 'operating hours' and 'open 24x7' fields have no evident Overture carrier and should be treated as unresolved rather than assumed fillable.

verdict_summary:
All 20 claimed URLs are live (HTTP 200) — no 404s, no dead links. But "verified_live=true" was doing less work than it appears: on two entries it certified only that a JavaScript shell rendered, and on one it was reported from intent rather than from the actual response. Verdicts: 11 CONFIRMED, 8 PARTIAL, 1 REFUTED.

THE REFUTED ITEM — YellowPages.com robots.txt. The researcher recorded access=scrape_prohibited / tos=prohibited citing robots.txt. The file says the opposite for a self-identifying crawler: "User-agent: *" / "Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-train=no,use=reference" / "Allow: /". Only nine named AI bots are Disallowed. This project's polite_get UA would match the permissive "*" rule. I tried to rescue the conclusion from the ToS instead — yellowpages.com/about/legal/terms-of-use returns HTTP 403, and the parent Thryv terms page yielded no scraping clause. So the prohibition is unproven on the cited evidence and unverifiable on the ToS. Not scraping YellowPages remains the right call (proprietary aggregated directory, no licence granting redistribution, and an express ai-train=no reservation), but the reason recorded in the source registry must be corrected — writing "robots.txt forbids it" would itself breach the repo's honesty rules.

THE MOST DAMAGING NEAR-MISS — Mapillary licence. It was registered flatly as CC BY-SA. The ToS continues "...unless we indicate otherwise... (such as the Creative Commons Attribution NonCommercial Share Alike (CC BY-NC-SA license)". Some imagery is non-commercial-restricted, and §12 adds further commercial-use terms the researcher never mentioned. A blanket CC BY-SA row is precisely the wrong-licence error class. Per-image licence must be read at fetch time.

MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OMISSION — ODbL §4.4(c). The researcher's fallback ("if ODbL route geometry must be used, restrict output to §4.5 Produced Works") is unsafe as written. §4.4(c) states a Derivative Database "is Publicly Used and so must comply with Section 4.4 if a Produced Work created from the Derivative Database is Publicly Used" — the carve-out does not survive once a Derivative Database has been formed, and §4.6 then compels handing over a machine-readable copy. This makes the public-domain routes recommendation load-bearing, not merely preferable.

ALSO CORRECTED: Yelp is no longer a free-key API — §7.1 gives a 30-day trial then a paid month-to-month subscription (§8.1), with §7.3 barring public launch during the trial, so it fails the no-paid-API constraint independently of its 24-hour storage cap (that cap itself is CONFIRMED verbatim, as is the Display Requirements "Store data longer than 24 hours" ban). Justdial's robots.txt is not a blanket ban either, though it does specifically Disallow /us/ — and it is an India directory, out of scope regardless. Google's March-2025 page still leaves a real free tier (10,000 Geocoding req/mo), so the disqualifier there is the ToS, not the price.

STRONGEST WORK, INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED: the taginfo/Overpass WhatsApp finding matched to the digit (17,937 / 117 / 813), and my own Overpass re-run returned total=0 US repair shops with any WhatsApp tag at 2026-07-23T09:02:21Z. All four Google §3.2.3 sub-citations, both OSMF guidelines, ODbL §4.4/4.5/4.6, CDLA-2.0, FSQ Apache-2.0 and the Maps-URLs keyless claim are verbatim-accurate. Overture's per-theme mapping is exactly right, with the operational nuance that Places carries no theme-level licence at all — it is a seven-provider CDLA/Apache/CC0 mix, so per-row licence tracking is mandatory.

NET UPGRADE FOR THE BUILD: I resolved the BTS NHFN from a JS shell to a real service — services.arcgis.com/xOi1kZaI0eWDREZv/.../NTAD_National_Highway_Freight_Network/FeatureServer/0, count=12989 polylines (not "unknown"), public domain confirmed from the service's own copyrightText, with ROUTEID/LNAME/SIGN* supplying route_id and route_name and BEGMP/ENDMP supplying milepost referencing for nearest_route_point. Vintage is "Version 2023.02.08", so observed_at must be 2023-02-08. The routes table is buildable, contamination-free, today. One unresolved gap neither of us can fill from the checked sources: Overture Places has no opening-hours field, so "operating hours" and "open 24x7" should be marked unresolved rather than assumed fillable.
